coordinateNote: Coordinates from three sources: the exported XLSX data (13 places), the GSI address-search API (23 places), and Wikipedia (1 place). Pins are address-level approximations, not verified entrances. Check opening hours and reservations directly with each shop.

start.name: Koenji Station
start.heading: Start at the north exit
start.blurb: Six minutes from Shinjuku on the Chūō Line. The student movements of the sixties settled here, punk followed the cheap rent through the seventies, and neither the bubble nor the 2022 redevelopment plans managed to move any of it on — so the streets still look like the seventies left them. North side first, bakery in hand, then under the tracks and down the arcades. Two endings at the bottom; pick by where you want to drink.

branches.name: Mabashi Inari
branches.heading: The small-rooms ending
branches.blurb: The village shrine with the twin-dragon basin, west of everything and usually empty. Inari is the kami of commerce, which makes it the right one to thank after a day of buying things. Then back north into Daiichi Market, where every room is tiny: six counter seats at Metal Meshi, a rock bar next door to a shop selling ornamental fish and open until 2am, and Baka Doshi further up the north side.

branches.name: Koenji Hikawa
branches.heading: The Weathering with You ending
branches.blurb: The weather shrine at the far south edge. Kisho Shrine sits inside the grounds — the only shrine in Japan dedicated to weather, where the ema are shaped like clogs because clogs were once used to forecast it, and where Weathering with You put its prayer for clear skies. Then the climb back north into the big rooms: Jirokichi, Koenji High at around 250 capacity, and PI Stand if you would rather have a glass of wine than a support act.

sections.name: Koenji Station & North Side
sections.subtitle: The everyday side: bakery, cat shop, sento. Get oriented before you cross under the tracks.

sections.name: Daiichi Market
sections.subtitle: A postwar food market you enter through a greengrocer. Spice curry, used clothes, a rock bar that sells fish.

sections.name: Koenji Pal Shopping Street
sections.subtitle: The covered arcade: vintage by the storefront, zakka in the corners, two cafes worth sitting down in.

sections.name: Etoile Shopping Street
sections.subtitle: The cross street heading west off the spine. Burgers, serious coffee, lasagna, and a wine bar for when it gets late.

sections.name: Look Shopping Street
sections.subtitle: The vintage spine. Nearly one in four storefronts sells secondhand, all the way to Shin-Koenji.

sections.name: Kōnan-dōri
sections.subtitle: The live-house strip east of the arcade, and the Awa Odori route — the biggest outside Tokushima, dancing through here the last weekend of August.

sections.name: Koenji Hikawa Shrine
sections.subtitle: The southern edge of the walk.

spots.name: Reuse Select Tifana Koenji
aliases: リユースセレクト ティファナ 高円寺店
spots.description: Reuse shop on the north side. Worth a fast pass on the way to the market; the stock turns over constantly.
spots.note: Coordinates from the exported XLSX data.

spots.name: Kosugiyu
spots.description: The neighborhood sento. A working public bathhouse, not a tourist version of one.
spots.note: Coordinates from the exported XLSX data.

spots.name: Floresta Koenji
spots.description: The animal-doughnut shop: organic ingredients, cute shapes, and doughnuts that actually taste good. An easy sugar stop on the north side.
spots.note: Coordinates from the exported XLSX data.

spots.name: Nekonohaitai
spots.description: A narrow cat-goods shop on Junjo street, packed floor to ceiling with cat art and bric-a-brac. You will know it when you see it.
spots.note: Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: Hattifnatt
aliases: ハティフナット高円寺
spots.station: Koenji (JR Chuo / Sobu), 4 min walk from north exit
spots.description: A cafe wrapped floor to ceiling in Marini Monteany's animal murals. The vegetarian taco rice and a cassis float make a good lunch before the vintage stretch. Cute without being precious about it.
spots.note: Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: Koenji Baka Doshi
spots.description: A north-side bar. The name translates roughly to 'a bunch of idiots,' which is about right for a last drink after you come back across the tracks.
spots.note: Coordinates from the exported XLSX data.

spots.name: Shigekuniya 55 Bakery
spots.station: Koenji (JR Chuo / Sobu), 2 min walk from north exit
spots.description: The bakery everyone points you at, on the market block northwest of the north exit. The bread really is that light and fluffy, and the morning queue is real. Regularly ranked among the best in the city, and it earns it.
spots.note: Coordinates from the exported XLSX data.

spots.name: Curry Shop Kujira
aliases: カリーショップくじら 高円寺
spots.station: Koenji (JR Chuo / Sobu), 1.5 min walk from north exit
spots.description: Spice curry hidden inside the market. The entrance runs through a green grocer down a back alley, which is about as Koenji as it gets. Nine counter seats and a line at lunch. The three-curry plate is the move: chicken, beef keema, and pork vindaloo on one tray. Tabelog's Curry 100 six years running, founded 2011.
spots.note: Named in the walking video transcript as 'Kuira Kuji' (transcription error). Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: ibeestore
spots.station: Koenji (JR Chuo / Sobu), 1 min from the north exit
spots.description: Designer secondhand rather than general used clothing — Burberry, Kenzo and the like, selected rather than racked by the metre. Buy-and-sell, ten years in Koenji this year, and three branches in the area, so what does not fit one shop turns up in another. A minute from the north exit.
spots.note: Speciality confirmed from the shop’s own Instagram.

spots.name: Rock Bar Heaven
spots.station: Koenji (JR Chuo / Sobu), 1.5 min walk from north exit
spots.description: The medaka pub. A rock bar beside a shop selling ornamental killifish, because Koenji. Open until 2am, which makes it the honest last stop.
spots.note: Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: Ripcel Koenji Station Front
aliases: リプセル 高円寺駅前店
spots.description: A buyback counter for brand bags, watches and jewelry just south of the gates, at the top of the Pal block. Saved it, still have not been inside.
spots.note: Despite the 'station front' name the shop is on the south side; an earlier geocode attempt with a bad address string resolved roughly a kilometre east-southeast of the station. Coordinates from GSI geocoder with the correct address.

spots.name: Live Music JIROKICHI
spots.description: Opened in 1975 as an izakaya called Namaiki Sakaba Jirokichi and never entirely stopped being one. Blues, jazz and soul cross here rather than any single scene — fifty years of it this year, built on cheap rent and a six-minute ride to Shinjuku.
spots.note: Coordinates from the exported XLSX data.

spots.name: Atlantis Vintage Tokyo
spots.description: Vintage luxury bags inside the arcade. Deep stock, clean condition, staff who leave you alone until you need them. The kind of shop people come to Koenji specifically for.
spots.note: Located in Koenji Pal Shopping Street. Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: BAZZSTORE Koenji Pal
aliases: バズストア 高円寺パル商店街店
spots.station: Koenji (JR Chuo / Sobu), 2 min from the south exit
spots.description: Brand secondhand alongside plain casual and fast fashion, about 5,000 pieces over one floor up. The buyback counter is the point: this is where the neighbourhood sells its clothes, so stock turns constantly. Open noon to 10pm every day of the year, buyback until 9:30.
spots.note: Coordinates from the exported XLSX data.

spots.name: TreFac Style Koenji 3
aliases: トレファクスタイル 高円寺3号店
spots.description: Treasure Factory's clothing-only format, a few steps east of the Pal arcade on the parallel street. Organised racks and fixed prices rather than a dig, which makes it a useful calibration stop before the small shops. Stays open past 8pm when most of Pal has shut.
spots.note: Coordinates geocoded from the official branch address.

spots.name: R-za Dokushokan
spots.station: Koenji (JR Chuo / Sobu), 4 min walk from south exit
spots.description: A reading cafe with a strict no-talking rule: fifteen hundred books, plants everywhere, nine seats and each one is different. One has a fish tank. One has crystals. One hides a diorama in the drawer. The stairwell is nothing, then the second floor opens up like a Ghibli set. Noon to 10pm, closed Mondays.
spots.note: Named in the walking video transcript as 'Arza Douan' (transcription error). Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: Meikyoku Kissa Renaissance
aliases: 名曲喫茶ルネッサンス
spots.description: A meikyoku kissa, the classical-record cafe Japan does better than anyone. Twenty-five hundred LPs; you write your request on a blackboard and the owner plays it. The coffee is called Highlight Coffee because it is strong. She took over the records and fittings when the original Meikyoku Kissa Classic closed in 2005 and has run it since 2007. Noon to 7:30pm (weekends to 9:30), closed Mon-Tue.
spots.note: Named in the walking video transcript as the 'classical record cafe.' Coordinates from Wikipedia.

spots.name: Hachimakura
spots.station: Koenji (JR Chuo / Sobu), 3 min walk from south exit
spots.description: A shop devoted entirely to vintage paper: old labels, tickets, postcards and packaging from Japan and abroad, treated like the design objects they are. The owner buys in Europe and also commissions reproductions made with traditional craftsmen. 1 to 9pm (8pm Sundays), closed Mon-Tue.
spots.note: Named in the walking video transcript as the 'vintage paper shop.' Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: Razani-ya Koenji
aliases: ラザニ屋 高円寺店
spots.description: Seven kinds of lasagna, which is a strange hill to die on and a good one. The signature runs a three-day meat sauce under bechamel on chewy fresh pasta; there is also gorgonzola-duck, a green lasagna, and one under an omelet. 1,340 yen, eat in or take away.
spots.note: Named in the walking video transcript as the 'lasagna restaurant.' Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: Dealer Ship
spots.description: Second-floor vintage housewares. A serious Fire-King and Pyrex collection, American glass in rare shapes and clean condition.
spots.note: Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: Don Don Down on Wednesday
aliases: ドンドンダウン オン ウェンズデイ
spots.description: Nothing here has a price tag. Every piece carries a vegetable sticker that you match against a board on the wall, and every Wednesday each sticker drops a tier: 2,000 yen becomes 1,500, then 900, and eventually 100. Come on a Wednesday or don't bother.
spots.note: Coordinates from the exported XLSX data.

sources.label: Don Don Down — how the markdown works

spots.name: Menosuyama
spots.address: 1F Dai-2 Shimoda Building, 4-24-1 Koenjiminami, Suginami, Tokyo
spots.description: Rare agave and collector plants plus artist-made pots, with a repotting service. A shop this specific is the whole point of the back streets. 1 to 6pm, closed Wednesdays.
spots.note: Named in the walking video transcript as the 'agave shop.' Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: BE-IN RECORDS
spots.description: Blues and classic rock vinyl with a whole section set aside for the British sixties and seventies. Stones and Beatles people will be here a while.
spots.note: Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: Substore Base
spots.description: The stripped-back counterpart to BE-IN: a lifetime of punk and metal condensed into one small room, from the canon to the truly obscure.
spots.note: Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: Koenji Metal Meshi
spots.description: A heavy metal dining bar where every dish is named after a band: Master of Nuggets, Avocado Dry Curry, Saba Bloody Saba. One chef, six counter seats, cash only, 6 to 9pm, closed Thursdays. Works as dinner if the west shrine is your ending.
spots.note: Named in the walking video transcript as the 'heavy metal restaurant.' Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: Awajishima Burger Koenji
aliases: 淡路島バーガー高円寺店
spots.address: 1A Kitaichi Building B, 3-49-5 Koenjiminami, Suginami, Tokyo
spots.description: Burgers built on sweet Awaji Island onions, inside the old arcade. Crispy onion rings, four small tables. The street was named for a theater that used to stand here; the burger shop is its own landmark now.
spots.note: Located in the Etoile Shopping Arcade. Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: RAD BROS CAFE
spots.description: The best find on the east side. Single-origin coffee, lovely staff, and a cherry-chocolate cheesecake that is honestly one of the best slices I have had in Tokyo. Small room; go before the afternoon rush.
spots.note: Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: PI Stand
spots.description: A compact bistro and wine bar with a rotating pan-Asian menu: sea bream carpaccio with kumquat, tiny banh mi sliders. Light plates, relaxed room, friendly staff. The right palate cleanser after a day of vintage shops.
spots.note: Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: Small Change Koenji
spots.description: A bar near the top of Look. The natural landing after the long vintage stretch, especially coming back east from Mabashi.
spots.note: Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: TreFac Style Koenji
aliases: トレファクスタイル 高円寺店
spots.description: The original Koenji branch of the same chain, and the one people mean when they say TreFac. Bigger floor than the Pal branch. It sits about 250m east of Look, so it is a deliberate detour rather than something you pass.
spots.note: Off the walking spine — roughly four minutes east of Look.

spots.name: Koenji High
spots.description: The biggest live house in Koenji, open since 2008. Shoegaze and indie are home turf and Tokyo Shoegazer is a fixture. About 280 capacity, proper sound, and a cafe called AMP on the ground floor.
spots.note: Named in the walking video transcript. Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: KIKI
spots.description: The original shop, and the more focused of the pair: 70s American ladies' vintage, dresses and separates with the bric-a-brac to match. It sits far enough down Look to prove the point that the street runs all the way to Shin-Koenji — most people turn back long before.
spots.note: Coordinates from the exported XLSX data.

spots.name: KIKI2
spots.description: Vintage clothing shelved in among American toys, which is exactly as chaotic as it sounds. The first of the two KIKI shops you reach walking south down Look.
spots.note: Coordinates from the exported XLSX data.

spots.name: Top of the Hill Koenji
spots.description: The far south bar. If you end at Hikawa, this is where the climb back north starts.
spots.note: Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

spots.name: Mabashi Inari Shrine
spots.description: A small Inari shrine that feels borrowed from a village: a long sheltered approach, portable shrines stored behind glass, and one of only three torii in Tokyo with dragons climbing and descending the pillars. This corner was farmland until 1923, when farmers subdivided it for laborers and merchants displaced by the Great Kanto Earthquake.
spots.note: Coordinates from the exported XLSX data.

spots.name: Koenji Hikawa Shrine
spots.description: Inside the grounds sits Kisho Jinja, Tokyo's only weather shrine, the one Makoto Shinkai drew for Weathering with You. The Imperial Army's forecasters founded it during the war; after 1945 it should have been dissolved with the other state shrines, so it was quietly moved here instead. The ema are painted with sandals, a nod to the old ritual of forecasting the weather by throwing them.
spots.note: Coordinates from GSI geocoder.

breaks.title: First stop — coffee at the top
breaks.subtitle: About 500m in, where Junjō runs out and you turn back
breaks.blurb: You have walked the north side and the shops thin out. Both of these are cafes rather than anything heavier — sit down before you commit to the market.

breaks.title: Lunch — in the market
breaks.subtitle: Back down among the stalls, before you cross the tracks
breaks.blurb: The one meal on this walk worth planning around. Nine counter seats and a queue; the bakery is the fallback if the queue is long.

breaks.title: Sit down properly — the kissa
breaks.subtitle: Roughly 1.2km in, at the bottom of the arcade
breaks.blurb: Neither of these is a coffee you take away. One bans talking and hands you a book; the other plays whatever record you write on the blackboard. Budget an hour.

breaks.title: Late lunch — heading west
breaks.subtitle: On Etoile, the last proper food before the shrine
breaks.blurb: Etoile is where the walk turns west. Eat here or you are going to the shrine hungry.
